description.narrative: Project Development Objective (from Project Appraisal Document) The Project Development Objective is to improve forest management; and increase access to markets and basic services by small forest producers including indigenous and campesinos in selected Northern Provinces of Argentina

The project development objective of the Forests and Community Project for Argentina is to improve forest management; and increase access to markets and basic services by small forest producers (including indigenous people and campesinos) in selected Northern Provinces. This project is comprised of five components. (1) The sustainable livelihoods component will improve the livelihood of small forest producers and promote sustainable forest landscape management, with special emphasis on the Chaco Ecoregion, through: (a) the preparation of Integrated Community Plans (PICs); (b) the implementation of PICs; and (c) the design and implementation of subprojects. (2) The natural forest management and civil society component will support carrying out of a national forest and climate awareness campaign to expand and maintain support for the implementation of the Forest Law through the establishment and/or expansion of existing community radio to distribute information on sustainable natural resources management, climate resilience and indigenous rights. (3) The skills development and technology transfer component will finance strengthening the technical, managerial skills of: (i) indigenous and campesino community members; (ii) small forest producers; and (iii) technical service providers and extension agents working in the Selected Northern Provinces, through the provision of short training courses including both classroom and community level instruction and financing of scholarship grants. (4) The forest monitoring component will support the expanding Secretariat of Environment and Sustainable Development (SAyDS) technical and institutional capacity to manage forest information and monitor changes in forest cover. (5) The project management and impact monitoring component will finance: (i) provision of support for the technical and administrative coordination of the project, (ii) development of an impact evaluation system to identify changes in outcomes directly attributable to Project activities and (iii) development and implementation of a grievance redress mechanism to identify and resolve Project related grievances.

comment.narrative:
<p>Of the 10,441 beneficiaries reported, 4887 correspond to female beneficiaries and 6826 correspond to indigenous beneficiaries. </p>
<p>End target is 10,500 beneficiaries according to the approved project restructuring</p>

title.narrative: 1.2. Households with improved access to water for consumption and production

comment.narrative: <p>1,985 households have reported improved access to water for consumption or production through the construction of 40 rainwater-collection roofs and the construction of 46 excavated reservoirs (198.5% of the final goal of 1,000 of the Intermediate Result Indicator (IR) 1.2 Indicator).</p>

<p>Out of the 88 Comprehensive Community Plans (PICs) which preparation concluded, 82 were approved by the provincial authorities, 6 have been at technical evaluation phase by the provincial authority of Chaco. Out of the 82 PICs approved by the provincial authorities, 2 were approved since November 2021 (both from Santiago del Estero Province).</p>
<p>2,599 households (1,675 indigenous, and 924 "campesinos") were formally linked to Law 26.331 due to the Project, through the approval of 82 PICs. These beneficiaries represent 124% of the Project's final goal. </p>

title.narrative: Forest area brought under management plans

comment.narrative: <p>The total area of formulated PICs is 384,380 hectares, reaching 91.5% of the PDO indicator target. </p>

title.narrative: 2.3. Share of volume of timber transported in participating provinces tracked by SACVeFor

comment.narrative:
<p>The current value reported reflects the accumulated volume of timber transported and recorded under SACVeFor (1.449.919 tons) since the beginning of CY2020, as a proportion of the baseline value.</p>
<p>51.36% of the volume of wood (744,682 tons) definedas the baseline has been registered (by Jujuy, Salta, Santiago del Estero and Chaco) through the Control and Verification Administration System Forestry (SACVEFOR) in 2021 (the final goal (50% of 1,449,919 tons for Indicator RI 2.3 has been reached). Likewise, it was reported that from January 1 to March 21, 2022 124,318 tons of wood have been registered (8.57% with respect to the baseline). However, this result is achieved with only 4 of the 10 targeted Provinces that were expected to have reported timber transported to SAVCEFOR at the end of the Project. Additionally, it is noted that the province of Chaco registers 96% of all the registered volume, which is consistent with the historical records.</p>

title.narrative: 1.3. Small forest producers that increase trade agreements

comment.narrative: <p>546 small producers have established agreements for the commercialization of their forest products (91% of the final goal of 600 of Indicator RI 1.3).</p>

title.narrative: People in forest and adjacent community with monetary and non-monetary benefit from forest

comment.narrative: <p>5,770 indigenous and campesinos have benefited from project investments (equipment, trainings, technical support, etc.) and have improved their monetary and non-monetary benefits from forests, reaching 55% of PDO Indicator target.</p>

title.narrative: Small forest producers reporting improved access to markets

comment.narrative: <p>620 Small Forest Producers have reported (through surveys) an improvement in access to markets (representing 103.3% of the final goal of 600).</p>

title.narrative: 3.2. Beneficiaries that feel project investments reflected their needs (percentage)

comment.narrative: <p>1083 households (81.1%) of 1336 households surveyed expressed satisfaction of expectations (83% women and 80% men); compared to 75.5% reported in April 2021 and to the final goal of Indicator RI 3.2, which points to 70% of all beneficiary women and 70% of men beneficiaries of the Project.</p>

title.narrative: 1.4. Integrated Community Plans formulated with resources from provinces

comment.narrative:
<p>3 PICs were formulated and approved jointly between MAyDS and the provincial authority of Chaco (15% of the final goal of 20 PICs formulated jointly from IR 1.4), and 6 more PICs were prepared in the same way for provincial evaluation.</p>

<p>46.7% of the beneficiaries ???of the project are women (4,887) and 65.3% are indigenous (6,826) (Indicator IR 3.1).</p>

<p>In the same way, MAyDS reported that 81.1% of the 1,335 households surveyed until the last implementation support mission (1,083; 83% of the womensurveyed, 80% of the men surveyed and 71% of the indigenous people surveyed) stated that the Project's investments met their needs (the final goal of Indicator IR 3.2 aims for 70% of the total women beneficiaries and 70% of the men beneficiaries of the Project to do so).</p>

<p>As part of the progress achieved in the implementation of the approved PICs, MAyDS reported that:</p>

<p>(i) out of the 15 deep groundwater drilling works being constructed to increase access to water in Santa Victoria Este, 13 had been completed, and 2 more are close to completion.</p>

<p>and (ii) 46 reservoirs were completed in Chaco and Santiago del Estero.</p>
<p>The Deforestation Early Warning System (SAT) is operational (the final goal of Indicator IR 2.1 has been reached), having generated 24.840 alerts until February, 2022.</p>

title.narrative: 2.2. Second national native forests inventory completed

comment.narrative: <p>The Second National Inventory of Native Forests has been completed and its results have been published.</p>
